newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Acer forges ties with China's Legend.
newsitem.headline: Acer forges ties with China's Legend.

text.p: Taiwan's computer giant Acer Inc said on Tuesday it would cooperate with China's computer maker, Legend, to make US$500 AcerBasic computers in the mainland.
"The deal unites the two largest players from their respective sides of the Taiwan Strait," a statement by Acer said.
Legend is China's largest domestic personal computer manufacturer, the statement said.
"Through the joint efforts of both companies, we believe we can sell more than 100,000 units in the first 12 months," Legend Group President Liu Chuanzhi said.
Acer launched the low-cost "network computer", an early entry in the industry's experiment with limited-function computer appliance, in Taiwan on June 18.
Acer has said AcerBasic would be marketed in developing countries. To save on costs, the machine can be plugged into a television set and does not come with a monitor.
The main central processing unit is a 100-megahertz chip from IBM Corp running Microsoft Corp's ageing Windows 3.1 and even older DOS operating software, Acer has said.
